title: India's Flag and National Symbols
summary: Learn the colours of our flag and the symbols that stand for our country.

steps.title: Our flag
sentences: The flag of India is called the Tiranga, which means tricolour.
It has three stripes: saffron at the top, white in the middle and green at the bottom.
In the middle of the white stripe is a blue wheel with 24 spokes, the Ashoka Chakra.

steps.title: What the colours mean
sentences: Saffron stands for courage and sacrifice.
White stands for peace and truth.
Green stands for faith, growth and the richness of the land.

steps.title: National symbols
sentences: The national animal is the tiger, and the national bird is the peacock.
The national flower is the lotus, the national fruit is the mango, and the national tree is the banyan.
The national river is the Ganga and the national aquatic animal is the Ganges river dolphin.

steps.title: National song and anthem
sentences: Jana Gana Mana is our National Anthem, and it takes about 52 seconds to sing.
Vande Mataram is our National Song.
We stand up straight and show respect when the anthem is played.

facts: The design of the flag was adopted on 22 July 1947, a few weeks before independence.
The Ashoka Chakra has 24 spokes, one for each hour of the day.
The Indian flag is traditionally made of khadi, hand-spun cloth.

quiz.q: What is the colour at the top of our flag?
How many spokes does the Ashoka Chakra have?

quiz.why: The peacock is the national bird.

notes: National symbols are as notified by the Government of India.
